objective: Learners analyze workplace mini-scenarios to identify likely unwritten expectations and name a reliable way to confirm them, so they learn to notice what a written policy doesn't say instead of guessing and hoping.
scenario: Given several provided workplace mini-scenarios illustrating a gap between a stated policy and its actual practice (arrival time, break usage, phone use), the learner states what the unwritten expectation likely is for each and names a specific, low-risk way to confirm it rather than guessing.
safetyNotes: All workplace mini-scenarios are provided and fictional; no real current or past employer needs to be described or judged.
materials: the provided set of workplace mini-scenarios

tasks.directions: Before analyzing, name one unwritten rule from any group setting you've been part of (school, a team, anything).

prompts.text: Think of any group you've been part of — what's one rule that everyone seemed to know but nobody actually announced?

tasks.directions: For each provided mini-scenario, state the likely unwritten expectation.

prompts.text: I stated the likely unwritten expectation for the arrival-time scenario.
I stated the likely unwritten expectation for the break-usage scenario.
I stated the likely unwritten expectation for the phone-use scenario.

tasks.directions: For each scenario, name a specific, low-risk way to confirm the expectation rather than guessing.

prompts.text: For each of the three scenarios, name a specific, low-risk way you could confirm the real expectation (for example, observing for a day, or asking a specific kind of question) rather than just guessing and hoping.

tasks.directions: Reflect on why unwritten rules exist.

prompts.text: Why do you think workplaces have unwritten expectations that differ from the posted policy at all, instead of just writing everything down?

remediation: If the learner's confirmation strategies are all the same generic 'just ask' with no specifics, reteach by modeling one concrete, low-risk confirmation method (such as watching what others actually do for the first day before assuming) and have them tailor a distinct method to each scenario.
extension: Have the learner write one additional workplace mini-scenario of their own invention with its own written-versus-actual gap, and analyze it the same way.
